title: Single-atom substitution redirects KatG reactivity from cofactor biogenesis to stereoselective sulfoxidation
task: Determine the role of tryptophan indole N–H in cofactor biogenesis and redirect heme reactivity via single-atom substitution
key_results: S-Trp105 substitution redirects KatG from Met–Tyr–Trp crosslink formation to enantioselective (S)-sulfoxide formation; 2.22 Å cryo-EM structure confirms S = O orientation toward iron
comments: The use of genetic code expansion to achieve atomic-level mechanistic interrogation is elegant and broadly applicable, though the physiological relevance of the redirected monooxygenase activity remains unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Indole N–H is essential for Met–Tyr–Trp crosslink formation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: N → S substitution prevents crosslinking and redirects to sulfoxidation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Single-atom substitution can reroute distal heme site reactivity from radical to two-electron chemistry
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: S-Trp undergoes heme-dependent two-electron oxygen-atom transfer versus native one-electron radical chemistry

title: Intrinsic DNA codes govern distinct modes of nucleosome-transcription factor interactions
task: Identify DNA sequence codes governing nucleosome positioning and transcription factor binding modes
key_results: Four distinct nucleosomal DNA classes identified; ΔNPS values correlate closely with in vitro nucleosome occupancy; four distinct modes of nucleosome–TF interaction mapped
comments: The work elegantly shifts focus from protein-centric to DNA-centric mechanisms, though causality between DNA patterns and nucleosome positioning versus TF binding preference remains to be fully established.

model_io.model: Nucleosome positioning and TF binding analysis
inputs: human genome sequences (in vivo and in vitro)

hypotheses.hypothesis: DNA sequence patterns (WW/SS and anti-WW/SS) encode information for nucleosome positioning and TF binding
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: patterns are associated with TF binding in chromatin and correlate with nucleosome occupancy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Different DNA codes exhibit distinct rotational offsets
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: nucleosomes sharing same pattern are rotationally in phase; different patterns show specific offsets

title: Extracellular matrix stiffness determines the phenotypic behavior of dedifferentiated melanoma cells through a DDR1/2-dependent YAP mechanotransduction pathway
task: Define ECM stiffness-mediated phenotypic plasticity in dedifferentiated melanoma via DDR1/2-YAP signaling
key_results: Dedifferentiated cells showed heightened YAP activation and increased proliferation/migration/invasion on stiff collagen; soft ECM restored BRAF/MEK inhibitor sensitivity; DDR1/2 and YAP inhibition suppressed stiffness-driven phenotypes
comments: The mechanotransduction axis is well-characterized, but the interplay between phenotypic plasticity and mechanoresponse across diverse tumor microenvironments remains clinically underexplored.

model_io.model: Melanoma cell subpopulations on collagen matrices of varying stiffness

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dedifferentiated melanoma cells are mechanosensitive and preferentially respond to ECM stiffness
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; increased spreading, focal adhesion maturation, YAP translocation, and proliferation/migration on stiff collagen

hypotheses.hypothesis: Soft ECM sensitizes dedifferentiated cells to BRAF/MEK inhibition
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; stiffness-modulated therapy resistance reversed by matrix softening

hypotheses.hypothesis: DDR1/DDR2-YAP signaling mediates mechanosensitivity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; genetic or pharmacological DDR/YAP inhibition suppressed stiffness responses

title: β-catenin-driven innate and metabolic reprograming in macrophages fuel T-cell-dependent inflammation in Toxoplasma gondii infection: implications for therapeutic intervention
task: Determine β-catenin-driven innate immunity and metabolic reprogramming in macrophages during Toxoplasma gondii infection
key_results: β-catenin ablation inhibited parasite replication; β-catenin-TCF4 drove IRF4→CYBB→ROS/mitophagy; elevated ROS activated AIM2-NLRP3 inflammasome; β-catenin promoted Warburg effect and M1 polarization; β-catenin deletion enhanced Th2/Treg responses and protected mice
comments: The mechanistic network integrating innate sensing, metabolic reprogramming, and adaptive immunity is comprehensive, though the non-canonical roles of β-catenin beyond TCF4 interactions warrant further characterization.

outputs: cytokine release (IL-1β, IL-12, IL-6, IL-23, TNF-α)

hypotheses.hypothesis: β-catenin signaling promotes T. gondii replication in macrophages
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; β-catenin ablation inhibits replication

hypotheses.hypothesis: β-catenin drives IRF4-mediated ROS production and inflammasome activation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; β-catenin-TCF4→IRF4→CYBB→ROS→AIM2-NLRP3-ASC-caspase-1-IL-1β cascade

hypotheses.hypothesis: β-catenin promotes M1 polarization and pro-inflammatory Th1/Th17 responses
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; β-catenin inhibition shifts to M2 phenotype and anti-inflammatory Th2/Treg responses

hypotheses.hypothesis: Macrophage-intrinsic β-catenin is required for parasite survival
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; β-catΔMΦ mice protected against infection

title: Characterization of membrane structures regulating primary ciliogenesis by quantitative isotropic ultrastructure imaging
task: Elucidate 3D membrane ultrastructures in primary cilium assembly
key_results: Identified tubular C-shaped and toroidal membrane intermediates; showed EHD1 promotes CP110/CEP97 removal via membrane tubulation
comments: Isotropic ultrastructure imaging is a powerful technical approach, though the functional significance of these novel membrane intermediates beyond ciliogenesis progression remains to be explored.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; observed formation of C-shaped and toroidal intermediates

hypotheses.hypothesis: EHD1 membrane tubulation promotes CP110/CEP97 removal
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; EHD1 directly regulates cap disassembly

title: The PLK4 inhibitor RP-1664 demonstrates potent efficacy in neuroblastoma preclinical models through a dual mechanism of sensitivity
task: Evaluate PLK4 inhibitor efficacy in TRIM37-gain neuroblastoma
key_results: RP-1664 showed robust anti-tumor activity in 14/15 xenografts; combined with chemoimmunotherapy maintained complete responses in 6/9 MYCN-driven models
comments: The dual mechanism (centriole amplification-driven multipolar mitosis and centrosome clustering defects) is elegant but the TRIM37-independent sensitivity pathway warrants deeper mechanistic investigation.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; hypersensitivity in patient-derived neuroblastoma lines

hypotheses.hypothesis: Centriole amplification drives sensitivity via multipolar mitosis and centrosome dysfunction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CRISPR screens and live imaging showed inability to cluster/inactivate supernumerary centrosomes

title: EZH2 as regulator of stemness signature and driver of esophageal squamous cell carcinomas

hypotheses.hypothesis: EZH2 acts via PRC2-independent mechanisms to regulate stemness
hypotheses.result: Suggested by molecular docking; direct validation needed

title: Koumine inhibits osteoclastogenesis and prevents ovariectomy-induced bone loss via suppression of the MAPK signaling pathways

hypotheses.hypothesis: Koumine does not impair osteoblast differentiation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; no cytotoxic effects on osteoblasts

title: MST1/Drp1 axis mediates microglia pro-inflammatory activation following cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury
task: Elucidate MST1/Drp1 axis in microglia pro-inflammatory activation during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury
key_results: Reperfusion elevated p-MST1 and p-Drp1(Ser616); MST1 inhibition decreased p-Drp1(Ser616) and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine release (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β); combined MST1/Drp1 inhibition reduced infarct volume and improved neurological function

hypotheses.hypothesis: MST1 activation drives Drp1(Ser616) phosphorylation during CIRI

hypotheses.hypothesis: p-MST1/p-Drp1(Ser616)-mediated mitochondrial fission promotes microglia pro-inflammatory activation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; MST1 and Drp1 inhibition suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine release and neuroinflammation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Drp1 overexpression reverses protective effects of MST1 knockdown

title: The embryo game uncovers hidden cell behaviours

key_results: Cell killing emerges as conditional strategy when embryo exceeds target size; killing/proliferation balance maintains optimal heX-embryoid size matching native disc

outputs: conditional killing strategy, proliferation rates, embryoid size regulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cell competition serves dual functions: error correction and size regulation via conditional killing as restrained threat
